verdict.rationale: x402 is documented as a per-request HTTP payment handshake: the server quotes a price in a 402 response and the client signs and retries. Its docs explicitly describe charging "without checkout pages", and nothing in the pack shows a protocol call to create or update a cart or order draft. The closest item is an integration that lets agents authorize payment sessions on a merchant checkout built on Payment Acceptance. That covers payment authorization, an adjacent capability, not cart or draft management.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my agent can create and update a cart or order draft through a documented protocol call
